verdict.tagline: Visceral co-op carnage survives a bloated footprint and technical friction.
for_you_if: you want intense cooperative shooter action
not_for_you_if: you are short on storage space
you need stable technical performance without crashes
you dislike microtransactions in older titles

distortion_flags.sentence: Positive sentiment increases significantly as playtime grows past the initial hours.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: New players face a confusing user interface and massive download sizes right away.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the user interface is a jumbled, rubbish mess and find it very difficult to figure out what to do as a new player.

citations.review_text: Interface is pretty rubbish - a jumbled mess. As a new player it's very very hard to figure out what to do. Also, I can't play it because it suddenly wont work.

I am a 55 year old biker and trucker father, and probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 16 now. My son got this game for from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 12 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he let me borrow his controller. Me and my son then played in turns and I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my son many happy memories.

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players note the enormous installation footprint.

claims.claim: The game has a massive installation file size ranging around 95 to 130 gigabytes.

citations.review_text: game literally too big to run in 2026. no texture optimization, and i learned all the DLC i had back then is just GONE.

✅ Massively improved from the first game
✅ Gameplay is very fun and satisfying
✅ Progression system feels very rewarding
✅ Several classes to play with
✅ Tons of unique weapons
✅ Highly replayable

❌ Game has no 'true' offline mode. There's an offline play mode but it's a broken misleading design - if you are not connected to the internet, you won't have any progression or your save file
❌ Time limited trader system still feels awful
❌ Game size is way too bloated (130 GB for a game that has no campaign and only 5 offline maps?)
❌ Melee combat felt inferior to first game
❌ Too many DLCs (some weapons are locked behind DLCs) and they're also overpriced (it's been a decade man it doesn't make sense to keep the price so high)
Why does this have to be almost 100 GB?

Massive downgrade from the first game.

Pros :
- Different zed variants and bosses
- New classes with special perks/talents
- Dosh physics colllision

Cons :
- Gunplay feels less satisfying
- Bad atmosphere (the dark, gloomy ambience of KF1 is gone)
- The music is definitely not as good as in KF1
- Horrible, cringe-worthy voicelines
- Fortnite-like almost childish animations
- Guns sound weaker
- 95gb 

I'll stick with KF1.
It goes on sale for pocket change cheap if you still want to try it out.

Very cool upscale of Killing Floor 1 & compatibility with the ROG.
Almost 30$ and 100gb doesn't make it appealing to get or download, however.

Solo play review:
All maps are well designed and some of the maps are exceptional, it is like fighting Zombies across the multiverse. The weapon variety is decent. Visual and audio effects are significanlty superior to Killing Floor 1 from 2009. It is worth the 94 GB space requirement. It is very convenient to jump into this game for  10-15 minutes, finish a map and then quit the game and back to your life. 

The game runs very smooth even on my low end hardware. The game crashed only once in my 12+ hours of gameplay (first map, wave 3 within 10 minute of gameplay). It is intended to be a multi player game yet my experience in Solo was very satisfactory. I can only imagine the fun with multi player but I don't have such friends. Highly recommended on Sale.

claims.claim: Players experience technical issues where the game fails to launch or closes itself immediately.

citations.review_text: Is a very fun and charming game, unfortunately the game no longer allows me to launch it. You should not need to jump through hoops in order to play a game that you paid for and USED to work just fine.

used to play all the time and it was great but i tried again recently and it opens then closes itself and i tried for multiple hours to fix. I also know many of my friends have similar issues and we are on completely different pcs.

claims.claim: The game suffers from lag and stuttering issues even when running on hardware that exceeds recommended system requirements.

citations.review_text: ugh this game is a lag fest. seriously. even after messing with the config files and cranking everything down to absolute potato settings, it's still a stuttering mess. my pc ain't a supercomputer, i'll give you that, but it's well above the recommended specs. it *should* be running this without breaking a sweat. instead, it just chugs constantly.

The game constantly and severely lags even after configuring the files and playing on the lowest settings. My PC, of course, isn't super powerful, but it exceeds the recommended system requirements and should run the game without issues.

One of my absolute favorite games. Killing Floor 2 is an incredibly fun experience, especially with friends. There are tons of options (especially if you play with someone who has DLC) for different playstyles amongst the classes. Fast-paced action, and some stressful fights will keep you coming back for more. The community is pretty wholesome and helpful as well. 
The people who claim the game is dead are just plain wrong. KF2 has more active players than KF3 and KF1. It still receives updates and love from the devs, but not as much as it deserves (especially with the flop that is KF3).
Two negative aspects:
 1. the game size is massive for what it is. 
 2. There could be more variety amongst the zeds.
its a 90+ GB dead game not worth it
game is goated but please do something about the total file size

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game includes microtransactions and loot boxes.

citations.review_text: I love this game but it takes 5+ minutes to launch when it did launch, and now it doesn't launch at all, so I can't recommend. Also $40 for a 10 year old game is a scam, especially since there's DLC and microtransactions baked in.

Excellent zombie shooter game. It has so much progression across the perks to keep you entertained for dozens of hours. The new perks introduced in this one feel great and like a natural addition to the game. The loot box system is pretty scummy, but you don't have to interact with it much to make a cool looking guy. The community is very faithful tot his title. If you liked KF1, this is a worthy successor.

If you're going to buy a Killing Floor game. This is the game to buy. 

I was in the beta for Killing Floor 3, and my disappointment at seeing no changes being made to the game even after Tripwire said that they were going to reverse unwanted changes, like the specialist system for example, cannot be understanded. I was in highschool when they announced killing floor 2, and I remember getting so excited for this game, I made myself sick. Yeah, it's monetized to hell and back with ♥♥♥♥♥♥ little micro-transactions. But Killing Floor 2 is easily the best one in the series, if only by virtue of the fact that the first game was a gmod - mod more or less and the latest entry being unwanted slop that some dumb, probably balding executive at Tripware said "make call of dooty". That said, it easily stands on its own, having better gameplay, class designs, enemy designs, level designs, etc.  

Killing Floor 2 is objectively the best game in the series and you're doing yourself a massive disservice by wasting your time, and more importantly your money on the shameful, abandoned dumpster fetus that is Killing Floor 3.
